title: Serving others
hook: Eighty days ago, you needed help with everything. Now you have something to give.

screens.text: Remember your first week? Wudu felt complicated, the masjid felt big, and you didn't know where to sit. Eighty days later, you know a lot. Today is about turning around and helping: your masjid, your neighborhood, and the next person who says the shahada.

**Service is worship.** Allah tells believers to *"cooperate in righteousness and piety"* [Q 5:2, Saheeh Intl.]. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever eases someone's hardship, Allah will ease theirs [Muslim 2699].
bubbles: He also said every good deed is *sadaqah* (charity) [Bukhari 6021].
So stacking chairs after Jumu'ah, driving someone to the masjid or serving food at a shelter all count.

screens.prompt: Which of these count as serving others? Select all that apply.

options.text: Helping set up iftar at the masjid
options.feedback: Yes. Feeding people is one of the best deeds, and you'll meet people too.

options.text: Volunteering at a food bank in your town
options.feedback: Yes. Easing anyone's hardship counts, Muslim or not.

options.text: Sitting with a brand-new Muslim so they're not alone at Jumu'ah
options.feedback: Yes. You know exactly how much that matters.

options.text: Volunteering mainly so you can post about it for likes
options.feedback: Not quite. Deeds are judged by intentions [Bukhari 1]. Do it for Allah; posting can wait.

screens.text: **One body.** The Prophet ﷺ compared believers to one body: when one part hurts, the whole body feels it [Bukhari 6011]. And he said none of us truly believes until we want for others what we want for ourselves [Bukhari 13].
bubbles: Serving isn't only for Muslims, either. Kindness to neighbors and strangers is part of the same faith.

screens.text: Tap around the masjid. Every corner has a way to serve.

areas.entrance: Say salam to anyone who looks new or lost. You remember how that felt.
areas.shoes: Someone standing here after Jumu'ah, unsure where to go? Be the friendly face.
areas.hall: Stack chairs after Jumu'ah, or help set up iftar and events.
areas.wudu: Join a masjid cleanup. A clean, welcoming masjid is service too.

screens.situation: Tyler took his shahada at Dre's masjid last Friday. This Friday he's standing by the shoe racks after Jumu'ah, looking lost. Dre is three months in himself.

options.text: Say salam, tell Tyler he converted a few months ago too, and invite him to grab food with a couple of brothers
options.feedback: Yes. A friendly face who remembers the first week, plus a small group, is exactly what new converts say they needed.

options.text: Give him a list of twenty rules he should start following
options.feedback: Not quite. Overload is a top reason converts burn out. Friendship first; the rules come step by step.

options.text: Leave it to the imam; Dre's too new to help
options.feedback: Not quite. The imam can't be everywhere. Dre's recent experience makes him one of the best people to help.

options.text: Send Tyler a long list of online lectures
options.feedback: Not quite. Kind, but he needs a person more than a playlist right now.

screens.text: **You're an expert in the first 90 days.** Most converts say what they needed most was people: a salam, a meal invite, someone to sit with at Eid, patience with mistakes [Research Notes, Retention].
bubbles: Tell your imam you'd like to help welcome new converts.{teen} Under 18? Help through the masjid's youth program, never one-on-one in private.{/teen}
No teaching needed: just be the friend you needed.

Someone helped you get here. Now you get to pass it on.

check.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about easing someone's hardship?

options.text: Allah will ease the hardship of the one who does it
options.feedback: Right [Muslim 2699]. Service comes back to you.

options.text: It only counts if the person is Muslim
options.feedback: Not quite. Easing hardship is good with anyone; every good deed is charity [Bukhari 6021].

check.prompt: A new convert looks lost at the masjid. What helps most?

options.text: A warm salam, a little company, and an invitation
options.feedback: Right. People, not rules, are what new converts say they needed most.

options.text: A full list of rules to start on
options.feedback: Not quite. That overwhelms. Friendship first; learning comes step by step.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Cooperate in righteousness and piety [Q 5:2]; easing hardship is returned by Allah [Muslim 2699]; every good deed is charity [Bukhari 6021].
- Believers are like one body [Bukhari 6011]; want for others what you want for yourself [Bukhari 13].
- Intentions matter [Bukhari 1] (Day 62).
- Converts consistently say what helped most was people: a mentor, friends, an invitation, company at Ramadan and Eid; overload of rules is a leading reason for burnout [Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices; Yaqeen 2025: Muslim friends and mosque attachment are the strongest predictors of positive faith development].

**Likely questions**
- *"How can I volunteer at my masjid?"* Ask the mentor or office; common roles: setup and cleanup, iftar and Eid events, youth programs, welcoming visitors, food drives.
- *"How do I welcome a new convert?"* Say salam, share your own story briefly, invite them to something social, don't correct small mistakes, and connect them with the imam or mentor. Respect their privacy: never announce someone's shahada or Islam to others without their consent.
- *"I don't have much time."* Small and regular is best (Bukhari 6464, Day 29): a ride, a text, ten minutes after Jumu'ah.
- *"Does volunteering count as charity?"* Every good deed is charity [Bukhari 6021]; zakat is a separate, specific obligation (Day 46).

**Escalate:** anything involving a minor mentoring or meeting others (safeguarding policy, rule 12); volunteering situations that put the convert at risk.

**Don't**
- Don't push the convert to "do da'wah" or recruit; this lesson is service and welcome.
- Don't suggest a teen meet anyone one-on-one; route through the masjid.
- Don't pressure anyone who's in a hard season themselves; small acts count.
